Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 138 s. 2022 October 27, 2022 DIR. MARIA LOURDES AGUSTIN Regional Director, DILG-NCR Annex Building, Sugar Center Compound North Ave, Diliman, Quezon City Dear RD Agustin: This has reference to your letter dated October 3, 2022 asking for guidance on the request of Alabang Hills Village Homeowners Association Inc. (AHVHA) to revise and reconsider the legal opinion rendered by your Office on this issue: whether or not Barangay Cupang, Muntinlupa City, can issue a barangay clearance as requested by Mafiosa Farmstay Inc. (MFI) pending litigation with AHVHAI. Hereunder are the relevant antecedent facts which we have taken from the background provided in the documents forwarded to the Central Office: • The controversy is significantly connected with a case heard and deqided by the Regional Trial Court (RTC) in December 2021 , appealed to and decided by the Court of Appeals (CA), and is still subject to resolution of the motion for reconsideration filed before the CA. • The request for opinion was received by DILG-NCR on 20 April 2022 to which was responded to by the issuance of a Regional Office Opinion dated 30 May 2022. • The recent letter it received from AHVHAI requesting for the concerned regional office to revisit, revise and reconsider the opinion it issued was received last 1 July 2022. Said request was anchored on the following factual matters: 1. AHVAI filed a motion for reconsideration dated 09 December 2021 to the CA. 2. The government permits secured by MFI were declared null and void by the Muntinlupa City Building Official. • Your presented your findings as follows: 1. That level found that upon consultation of Punong Barangay Bulos with MFI and AHVHAI on the case at hand, the dispute was business- oriented and civil in nature. 2. MFI wanted to construct properties in the subject lot and AHVHAI wanted to purchase said properties but MFI refused. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

3. MFI wanted to use Don Manolo Boulevard as access/entry points to its property; however, due to business reasons, AHVHAI would not allow it and insisted to use the other road, V. Buecamino, as an access road. 4. Since Don Manolo Boulevard is the main thoroughfare that leads to and from Alabang-Zapote Road, the value of the properties along the road are high. 5. AHVHAI's refusal to allow MFI to gain access of D. Manolo Blvd. is due to the loss of profit that it would have garnered if only they had purchased the property of MFI. 6. The opinion rendered by that level was in accordance with the law and previous opinion of this Department. Barangay Cupang likewise emphasized that the Barangay issued the clearance to MFI on the basis of completion of the requirements set therefor. May we direct the attention on the fact that the litigation between MFI and AHVHAI involves an injunction and a prayer for a TRO against AHVHAI. It appears that the opinion on whether or not Barangay Cupang, Muntinlupa City can issue a barangay clearance depends on the decision of the then pending case. In view of the pendency of said case during the time the opinion was requested, the DILG Regional Office should have refrained from providing an opinion thereon to strictly comply with the sub judice rule. The fact that the opinion issued was in accordance with law and existing legal opinion is of no moment as violation of the sub judice rule is punishable by indirect contempt of court. Hence, our strict observance of this rule within the Department. The sub judice rule restricts comments and disclosures pertaining to the judicial proceedings in order to avoid prejudging the issue, influencing the court, or obstructing the administration of justice. A violation of this rule may render one liable for indirect contempt under Sec. 3(d), Rule 71 of the Rules of Court.l To remedy the situation at hand, you are hereby advised to re-evaluate whether the factual representation during the time the opinion was requested, as well as the contents of the assailed opinion, included an information and/or an acknowledgement that there is a pending case on the controversy. If it is in the affirmative, the concerned regional office may consider withdrawing said opinion with a justification based on the sub judice rule. The same does not equate to reversing the opinion thereon as it was based on the law and prevailing Department opinion. However, said action will prevent the attachment of liability to the issuing DILG Regional Office which may arise from violating the sub judice rule. On the other hand, if the pendency of said case came to the knowledge of the concerned regional office only after the issuance of the assailed DILG Regional Office's Opinion, withdrawing said opinion is not necessary. I G.R. No. 205956; 12 February 2014. Page 2 of 3

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Please be guided accordingly. BY o HORITY OF THE SECRETARY: V OR R. LLAMAS reta for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs JVRULLLS-LRALLD/kbm/clp
